en.title: 3. Qualification Tie-Break Rules
en.excerpt: Detailed hierarchy of tie-breaking calculations based on total scores, 10s count, and X count in accordance with World Archery rules.
en.content:
World Archery Tie-Break Order

When two or more archers finish qualification with identical total scores, Archeris automatically applies the official World Archery tie-break sequence:

  1. Total Score: Highest cumulative score across all qualification ends.
  2. Greater Number of 10s: Total count of arrows scoring 10 (including inner Xs).
  3. Greater Number of Xs: Total count of inner X-ring arrows.

Evaluating 10s vs Xs

Example: Archer A has 650 points with 24 tens and 8 Xs. Archer B has 650 points with 22 tens and 12 Xs. Archer A takes the higher seed because total 10s are evaluated before inner Xs.

Ties for Elimination Cut-off Positions

If athletes are tied on score, 10s, and Xs for the final qualifying spot (e.g., 16th place for a Top 16 bracket) or for a critical Bye position (e.g., 8th place), a field tie-break is required.

Field Shoot-Off & Coin Toss Resolution

The committee can resolve identical cut-off ties by conducting a single-arrow shoot-off or coin toss, manually adjusting the seeding order in the dashboard before bracket generation.
